title: A recent five-piece job and early guitar players
summary: He describes a recent July 4th job with Johnny McGee and friends, and recalls the Durfee brothers' small group from his beginnings.

story.theme_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section: instruments and players
story.community_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section's changing role

blocks.x: Around them Mommaloos in that area?

That's right. And we had Bill on bass, myself on trumpet, Johnny McGee playing clarinet, Tony Shrine on drums, and Sam Callie on guitar. You ever hear him play guitar? I think a long time ago with you. Oh man, he sounds like a piano man on a guitar. You don't need a piano, Paul, when you play with him. Really nice. He still plays nice.

Is it Gene Hemard or what is his name, Hemard? Gene Ory or whatever he tells himself he used to play with you some? He played guitar. I think he played with you or Red Hot. Maybe I got it confused. He played with Red Hot.

No, the only guitar man I played with was Lil Durfee. Durfee, that's years ago. I played with a little man. His brother played clarinet, he played guitar, Cat's Mastry played drum. I used to play trumpet.
What's his brother's name? Durfee, Frank Durfee. Frank Durfee is a guitar player? And which, wait a minute, I can't get this straight.

I can't remember whether Frank, no, Frank's brother played guitar. Frank was clarinet. I forget his brother's name. I can't remember. That's been many years ago. That's when I first started. I did. That's when we used to play Fireman's Hole over in Wiggle.
